instruction: Browse LEGO toys for kids and sort by lowest price.

metadata.explanation: Different toy brand (LEGO) with same category structure and sort order as original.
metadata.verification: Task uses existing check_direct_json_object metric and get_active_tab_html_parse getter. No custom functions needed. Evaluator checks breadcrumb navigation and URL parameters match expected product category and sort order.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: browsing LEGO toys for kids AND sorting by lowest price
Getter (get_active_tab_html_parse) can extract breadcrumb navigation from class 'pmpSearch_breadcrumb' to verify category filtering (LEGO/Toys/Kids)
Getter can extract sort selector text from class 'sbSelector' to verify price sorting selection
Getter performs dual verification using both HTML element extraction AND URL parameter checking (url_include_expected_multichoice) for robustness
URL parameter 'S=4' correctly corresponds to 'Price Low-High' sort order on Kohls.com
Metric (check_direct_json_object) correctly compares extracted result against expected values using exact boolean matching
Expected values are semantically correct: requires lego=true, toys=true, kids=true, price low-high=true, and is_other_exist=false
Complete coverage: verifies both navigation path (category filters) and sorting action
Logic flow is sound: accessibility tree → active tab URL → playwright navigation → HTML parsing → comparison
